# Building and pest inspection cost in Australia: 2026 examples

Published prices checked on 19 July 2026 were $499 plus GST in Perth, $500 plus GST in Melbourne and Brisbane, $595 including GST in Sydney, and $580 plus GST in Adelaide. Each example covers a slightly different job. Ask for an address-specific quote and make sure the roof space, subfloor, timber-pest inspection, written report and follow-up are clearly included.

## Research note
Official buyer guidance covers inspection scope, qualifications, insurance and report limitations. Start with the [NSW Government inspection checklist](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/inspecting-a-property/inspection-reports). The five city prices are provider-published examples accessed on 19 July 2026.

## Opening
### What the inspection fee includes
- **Access:** Does the fee cover the roof space, the subfloor, the sheds?
- **Report:** Building and timber pests, in writing, with photos, on time
- **Assurance:** Qualified, insured, and answering the phone afterwards

_A low fee can reflect a narrow job._

## Published price examples from five cities
We checked all five provider pages on 19 July 2026. Think of the figures as a useful snapshot, since the property, access and extras can all change the final quote.

**Provider-published combined building and pest inspection prices, accessed 19 July 2026**

| City | Published example | Scope or pricing note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sydney | [$595 including GST](https://csibuilding.com.au/prices/) | CSI lists an all-inclusive combined building and pest inspection price |
| Melbourne | [$500 plus GST](https://buildinginspectorsmelbourne.au/pricing/) | Residential house building and pest inspection |
| Brisbane | [$500 plus GST](https://buildingandpestinspectorsbrisbane.com.au/pricing/) | Residential house building and pest inspection |
| Adelaide | [$580 plus GST](https://aejbuildinginspections.com.au/prices/) | Residential combined building and pest inspection |
| Perth | [$499 plus GST](https://pierus.com.au/services/) | Combined inspection for a home up to 4 bedrooms by 2 bathrooms |

Ask for the fee at your actual address, because almost everything about a house can move it: the size, the storeys, the subfloor, the roof voids, the sheds, the age, the drive to get there, and how urgently you need the answer.

The [NSW Government advises buyers to check qualifications, professional indemnity insurance and report inclusions](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/inspecting-a-property/inspection-reports).

## The quote decoder
**Ask every inspector to answer the same fields**

| Field | What to ask | Why the answer changes value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Commissioning and reliance | Is the report addressed to me, and may I rely on it? | Reliance rights depend on the engagement terms |
| Building scope | Which structures and areas are included? | Garage, outbuildings, retaining walls, balconies and site may be excluded or limited |
| Timber-pest scope | Is a separate timber-pest inspection included, and to what scope? | Pest assessment needs an explicit scope |
| Access | Roof exterior, roof space, subfloor and restricted rooms, what is safely accessible? | Inaccessible areas remain blind spots |
| Methods | Visual inspection plus which meters or tools, used for what defined purpose? | Tools need access and defined interpretation |
| Report | Written report, photographs, significant items, limitations and delivery time? | A written report creates the decision record |
| Professional standing | Relevant qualification, state registration if applicable and professional indemnity insurance? | Requirements vary by state; insurance and competence need verification |
| Follow-up | Can I speak with the inspector, and is a reinspection available? | Clarification and changed access can matter before commitment |

## What moves the quote
- **Property form and size:** apartment lot, freestanding house, multi-level home, acreage, ancillary structures.
- **Access and safety:** low subfloor, roof pitch, locked or stored areas, height, confined spaces and weather.
- **Construction complexity:** mixed eras, additions, retaining structures, balconies, unusual materials or multiple roof voids.
- **Scope:** building only, timber pests, pool, invasive testing, specialist diagnostics or strata records are separate questions.
- **Timing and travel:** urgent auction turnaround, remote call-out, return visit and report deadline.

The quote should reflect the actual accessible scope. For apartments, combine the lot inspection with a [strata or owners-corporation records inspection](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/reading-your-owners-corporation-report).

## Understand the inspection limits
A conventional pre-purchase inspection is visual and non-invasive: the inspector looks hard at everything that can reasonably be reached, and opens nothing. Inside the walls, under fixed finishes, code compliance, full service testing and repair pricing all sit outside a typical scope. The report should identify its limitations and recommend further investigation for material issues.

Ask the inspector to name the agreed Australian Standard and scope in the engagement, then check that the report matches it. Standards documents themselves may require paid access.

## Vendor reports: test the rights as well as the content
For a vendor-supplied report, check its date, scope, access, commissioning party, inspector, professional indemnity insurance and purchaser-reliance or assignment terms. Commission your own inspection or specialist advice when reliance is absent, key areas were inaccessible or your concern sits outside scope.

## Allow for specialist follow-up
A good inspector states the limits of their scope clearly. Structural movement goes to an engineer, wiring to a licensed electrician, drainage to a plumber, suspect materials to a competent assessor, and air-quality questions to a defined indoor-environment scope. Leave time before the auction or the cooling-off deadline for that follow-up to happen.

## Choose the inspector you can rely on
A clear scope, good access and a useful conversation after the report can be worth far more than a small saving on the fee. Write down any blind spots before you commit. For an auction, use the [five-gate due-diligence plan](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/auction-day-due-diligence); for early triage, read about [desktop and physical report scopes](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/desktop-vs-physical-report).

> Important: Licensing and registration differ by state. Confirm qualifications, insurance, engagement terms, access, standard, pest scope and delivery before booking.

## Frequently asked questions
### How much does a building and pest inspection cost?
In a five-city sample checked on 19 July 2026, published combined-inspection examples were $499 plus GST in Perth, $500 plus GST in Melbourne and Brisbane, $595 including GST in Sydney, and $580 plus GST in Adelaide. Confirm the current address-specific fee and inclusions.

### Why do inspection prices vary?
Property size, storeys, age, safe roof and subfloor access, outbuildings, timber-pest scope, travel, urgency, report depth and follow-up all affect the fee.

### Is the cheapest inspection a bad one?
A low fee can still buy a useful inspection. Trace the price back to the scope: what was accessed, whether pests are included, what the written report covers, the inspector’s qualifications and insurance, and whether they will take your call afterwards.

### Does a building inspection include termites?
Timber-pest assessment needs an explicit scope. Ask how its findings and limitations will be reported.

### Is a vendor-supplied report useful?
Check date, scope, access, inspector, insurance and your purchaser-reliance or assignment rights. Commission more work where those terms leave material gaps.

### Does an apartment inspection cover the whole building?
A typical inspection focuses on the lot and accessible areas. Use the registered plan and scheme records for common-property condition, funding, insurance, defects and works.

### What extra inspections might be needed?
Only those prompted by material evidence or the property: for example structural engineering, electrical, plumbing/drainage, hazardous material, pool or indoor-environment work.

## Method
Government guidance on what an inspection covers, plus five real published prices from five cities, checked on the review date. Each figure keeps the GST basis and scope the provider stated.

## Limitations
Every quote reflects a particular property, access and scope. Use the examples as bearings, then get the current inclusions, insurance and timing in writing.

## Sources
- [Inspection reports before buying property](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/inspecting-a-property/inspection-reports) — NSW Government; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Due diligence checklist for home buyers](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/buying-and-selling-property/checklists/due-diligence) — Consumer Affairs Victoria; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Cost list](https://csibuilding.com.au/prices/) — CSI Building Inspections; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Pricing](https://buildinginspectorsmelbourne.au/pricing/) — Building Inspectors Melbourne; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Pricing](https://buildingandpestinspectorsbrisbane.com.au/pricing/) — Building and Pest Inspectors Brisbane; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Prices](https://aejbuildinginspections.com.au/prices/) — A E & J Building Inspections Adelaide; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Services and published prices](https://pierus.com.au/services/) — Pierus Building Inspections; accessed 2026-07-19

sections.heading: Qualifications and licensing vary by state
sections.markdown:

sections.heading: Ask for the engagement agreement before booking
sections.markdown:
The agreement should identify the client, property, inspection type, included structures, access basis, exclusions, fee, timing, report format and the terms governing reliance. The [AS 4349.1-2007 pre-purchase inspection standard](https://store.standards.org.au/product/as-4349-1-2007) provides a national framework for residential building inspections. Ask which standard and edition the service uses and how the agreed scope relates to it.

**Use the same questions for every quote**

| Question | A useful answer should identify |
| --- | --- |
| Who will attend? | The individual inspector, relevant experience and the business responsible for the report |
| What is included? | Dwelling, site, garage, outbuildings, retaining walls, balconies and agreed timber-pest scope |
| What access is attempted? | Roof exterior, roof space, subfloor, internal rooms and conditions that may prevent safe access |
| What is excluded? | Services, concealed areas, compliance, estimates and specialist matters outside scope |
| What will I receive? | Written report, photographs, significant findings, limitations, recommendations and delivery time |
| Can I ask questions? | A direct conversation with the inspector and a process for written clarification or reinspection |
| What protects the engagement? | Professional indemnity insurance, complaint process and clear reliance terms |

sections.heading: Independence should be easy to explain
sections.markdown:
Ask who recommended the inspector, who pays them and whether they have a financial relationship with the agent, vendor, report marketplace, repairer or pest-treatment provider. A referral can still lead to capable work; a clear answer lets you understand the relationship.

Consumer Affairs Victoria advises buyers to use an inspection service with professional indemnity insurance and to be cautious with a report offered by the seller or agent. Read the [Victorian inspection guidance](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property/inspect-properties-before-you-buy) before deciding whether a supplied report meets your needs.

sections.heading: Read a sample report
sections.markdown:
A sample reveals how the inspector thinks and communicates. Look for property-specific observations, useful photographs, precise locations, plainly stated access limits and recommendations that identify the next kind of expertise. A template can provide structure; the finished report should still feel like someone paid close attention to this home.

- **Clear significance:** the reader can tell what deserves attention first.
- **Visible limitations:** inaccessible areas are easy to find and understand.
- **Traceable photographs:** images have locations and connect to written findings.
- **Proportionate recommendations:** the next step answers a defined question.
- **Human follow-up:** the inspector is available to explain material findings.

sections.heading: Access often matters more than gadgets

Ask what safe-access conditions are needed for the roof exterior, roof space and subfloor, and who will arrange keys, hatches or permission. Tools such as moisture meters and thermal cameras can support defined observations. Their value depends on access, method, conditions and interpretation.

Put the quotes beside one another only after the inclusions line up. The [inspection-cost guide and quote decoder](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-and-pest-inspection-cost) provides current examples and a comparison framework.

sections.heading: Opening
sections.markdown:
### Findings and blind spots belong together
- **Observed:** What the inspector saw and where
- **Unresolved:** What access or scope could not settle
- **Next question:** Who can answer it before your deadline

_One material unknown can matter more than a long maintenance list._

sections.heading: Before the defect list, check the report itself
sections.markdown:
Confirm the property address, inspection date, weather, commissioning party, inspector and agreed scope. Check whether the report is addressed to you or gives you a documented right to rely on it. A useful report should make clear what was inspected, what could not be inspected and what kind of inspection was performed.

The [Australian Standard AS 4349.1-2007](https://store.standards.org.au/product/as-4349-1-2007) sets requirements for pre-purchase inspections of residential buildings. Read the report's own agreement and definitions as well, since the engagement may identify exclusions, additional services and property-specific limits.

sections.heading: Read it in five passes
sections.markdown:
1. **Scope:** which buildings, structures and inspection types were included?
2. **Access:** which roof, roof-space, subfloor, room, outbuilding or external area could not be reached?
3. **Significant findings:** which observations affect safety, structure, weatherproofing, timber pests or use?
4. **Recommendations:** which findings need clarification, monitoring, repair advice or a specialist?
5. **Decision:** what must be understood before the contract, cooling-off deadline or auction?

This order matters because findings and blind spots describe different risks. A visible leak is a finding. A roof space hidden by unsafe or restricted access is an unresolved area. Give both a place in the decision.

sections.heading: What common report language is telling you
sections.markdown:
**Translate the label into the next useful question**

| Report language | What it usually tells you | What to ask |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Major or significant defect | The inspector considers the consequence material within the report definition | What is the observed evidence, likely consequence and recommended next investigation? |
| Minor defect | A defect that may be localised, serviceable or less consequential | Does it need maintenance, monitoring or repair, and could several minor items share one cause? |
| Safety hazard | A condition the report identifies as presenting a safety concern | What immediate precaution and appropriately qualified trade or professional are recommended? |
| Further investigation | The observation cannot be resolved within the inspection scope | Who should investigate, what question should they answer and when is the answer needed? |
| Inaccessible or obstructed | The inspector could not observe a relevant area | Can access be arranged before commitment, and what uncertainty remains if it cannot? |
| Monitor | Change over time may be important | What should be measured or photographed, at what interval, and what change triggers escalation? |

Treat the report's definitions as controlling for that document. Ask the inspector to explain any label that changes your decision. The photograph shows an observation; the surrounding text should explain its location, context and significance.

sections.heading: Turn the report into a decision register
sections.markdown:
Create one line for every material finding and limitation. Record the location, evidence, consequence, open question, next person, deadline and any cost information you have. This keeps a worrying report readable and stops an important blind spot disappearing beneath a long maintenance list.

**A simple triage for unresolved findings**

| Signal | Useful next step |
| --- | --- |
| Movement with distortion, sticking openings or changing cracks | Ask whether a structural engineer should assess cause and significance; use the [wall-crack guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/cracks-structural-or-cosmetic) to organise the observations |
| Moisture, staining, mould or damaged finishes | Identify the water source and extent before pricing cosmetic work; follow the [moisture pathway](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/damp-and-moisture-in-your-home) |
| Active timber pests or evidence of damage | Clarify the timber-pest scope, activity, affected areas and recommended extent assessment |
| Suspect electrical, gas, plumbing or drainage condition | Use the appropriately licensed trade for that service and a clearly defined question |
| Roof space, subfloor or outbuilding not inspected | Seek safe access, a return inspection or a conscious allowance for the unresolved area |
| Possible asbestos or another hazardous material | Avoid disturbing it and use an appropriately competent assessor where identification affects the decision or planned work |

sections.heading: A report is a visual record with boundaries
sections.markdown:
A conventional pre-purchase inspection is generally visual and non-invasive over safely accessible areas. It does not open walls or prove the condition of every concealed element. Building condition, timber pests, electrical safety, plumbing, drainage, hazardous materials, approvals and legal rights may sit in different scopes.

The [NSW Government's buyer guidance](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/inspecting-a-property/inspection-reports) describes building, pest and strata reports as separate checks and recommends using a suitably qualified, insured professional. Use each report for its commissioned purpose and let its findings identify the next question.

sections.heading: Call the inspector while the inspection is fresh
sections.markdown:
- Which three findings deserve my attention first, and why?
- Which areas were inaccessible or only partly visible?
- Did any observations suggest one shared cause?
- Which recommendations should be completed before I commit?
- Which specialist should I brief, and what question should I ask?
- Would safe access or further documents change your view?

Write the answers into your decision register. If the response materially changes the written report, ask whether the inspector can confirm the clarification in writing.

sections.heading: Repairs and costs need a defined scope
sections.markdown:
A repair number becomes useful once the cause, extent and intended remedy are reasonably clear. Ask whether a figure in the report is an estimate, an allowance or a contractor quotation. Keep urgent safety work, investigation costs, near-term repairs and ordinary maintenance in separate lines.

For the inspection fee and inclusions, see the [2026 inspection-cost examples and quote decoder](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-and-pest-inspection-cost). If you are still appointing someone, use the [inspector selection guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/how-to-choose-a-building-and-pest-inspector).

sections.heading: Use the right deadline
sections.markdown:
Your useful deadline comes from the transaction: before signing, before a cooling-off period expires, or before bidding. Share material findings with your conveyancer or solicitor where they affect contract conditions, disclosure, settlement or the decision to proceed. At auction, work through the [five-gate due-diligence plan](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/auction-day-due-diligence) early enough to obtain specialist follow-up.

> Note: A good report does not make the decision for you. It gives you a dated set of observations, limitations and next questions so you can make the decision with your eyes open.

> Important: Urgent safety concerns and evidence of active water, pest activity or movement deserve prompt, property-specific advice. Avoid disturbing suspected hazardous material.

# How to read a building and pest inspection report, and what to do next

Start with the inspection scope and access limitations, then read the significant findings alongside the photographs and recommendations. Sort each unresolved issue by consequence, urgency and the person qualified to investigate it. A long defect list can include routine maintenance; one short limitation can hide a much larger uncertainty.

## Research note
A pre-purchase report records observations within an agreed scope and accessible areas. Read findings beside limitations and recommendations. The [Australian Standard](https://store.standards.org.au/product/as-4349-1-2007) sets national requirements, while the engagement and report define the service you received.

## Opening
### Findings and blind spots belong together
- **Observed:** What the inspector saw and where
- **Unresolved:** What access or scope could not settle
- **Next question:** Who can answer it before your deadline

_One material unknown can matter more than a long maintenance list._

## Before the defect list, check the report itself
Confirm the property address, inspection date, weather, commissioning party, inspector and agreed scope. Check whether the report is addressed to you or gives you a documented right to rely on it. A useful report should make clear what was inspected, what could not be inspected and what kind of inspection was performed.

The [Australian Standard AS 4349.1-2007](https://store.standards.org.au/product/as-4349-1-2007) sets requirements for pre-purchase inspections of residential buildings. Read the report's own agreement and definitions as well, since the engagement may identify exclusions, additional services and property-specific limits.

## Read it in five passes
1. **Scope:** which buildings, structures and inspection types were included?
2. **Access:** which roof, roof-space, subfloor, room, outbuilding or external area could not be reached?
3. **Significant findings:** which observations affect safety, structure, weatherproofing, timber pests or use?
4. **Recommendations:** which findings need clarification, monitoring, repair advice or a specialist?
5. **Decision:** what must be understood before the contract, cooling-off deadline or auction?

This order matters because findings and blind spots describe different risks. A visible leak is a finding. A roof space hidden by unsafe or restricted access is an unresolved area. Give both a place in the decision.

## What common report language is telling you
**Translate the label into the next useful question**

| Report language | What it usually tells you | What to ask |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Major or significant defect | The inspector considers the consequence material within the report definition | What is the observed evidence, likely consequence and recommended next investigation? |
| Minor defect | A defect that may be localised, serviceable or less consequential | Does it need maintenance, monitoring or repair, and could several minor items share one cause? |
| Safety hazard | A condition the report identifies as presenting a safety concern | What immediate precaution and appropriately qualified trade or professional are recommended? |
| Further investigation | The observation cannot be resolved within the inspection scope | Who should investigate, what question should they answer and when is the answer needed? |
| Inaccessible or obstructed | The inspector could not observe a relevant area | Can access be arranged before commitment, and what uncertainty remains if it cannot? |
| Monitor | Change over time may be important | What should be measured or photographed, at what interval, and what change triggers escalation? |

Treat the report's definitions as controlling for that document. Ask the inspector to explain any label that changes your decision. The photograph shows an observation; the surrounding text should explain its location, context and significance.

## Turn the report into a decision register
Create one line for every material finding and limitation. Record the location, evidence, consequence, open question, next person, deadline and any cost information you have. This keeps a worrying report readable and stops an important blind spot disappearing beneath a long maintenance list.

**A simple triage for unresolved findings**

| Signal | Useful next step |
| --- | --- |
| Movement with distortion, sticking openings or changing cracks | Ask whether a structural engineer should assess cause and significance; use the [wall-crack guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/cracks-structural-or-cosmetic) to organise the observations |
| Moisture, staining, mould or damaged finishes | Identify the water source and extent before pricing cosmetic work; follow the [moisture pathway](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/damp-and-moisture-in-your-home) |
| Active timber pests or evidence of damage | Clarify the timber-pest scope, activity, affected areas and recommended extent assessment |
| Suspect electrical, gas, plumbing or drainage condition | Use the appropriately licensed trade for that service and a clearly defined question |
| Roof space, subfloor or outbuilding not inspected | Seek safe access, a return inspection or a conscious allowance for the unresolved area |
| Possible asbestos or another hazardous material | Avoid disturbing it and use an appropriately competent assessor where identification affects the decision or planned work |

## A report is a visual record with boundaries
A conventional pre-purchase inspection is generally visual and non-invasive over safely accessible areas. It does not open walls or prove the condition of every concealed element. Building condition, timber pests, electrical safety, plumbing, drainage, hazardous materials, approvals and legal rights may sit in different scopes.

The [NSW Government's buyer guidance](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/inspecting-a-property/inspection-reports) describes building, pest and strata reports as separate checks and recommends using a suitably qualified, insured professional. Use each report for its commissioned purpose and let its findings identify the next question.

## Call the inspector while the inspection is fresh
- Which three findings deserve my attention first, and why?
- Which areas were inaccessible or only partly visible?
- Did any observations suggest one shared cause?
- Which recommendations should be completed before I commit?
- Which specialist should I brief, and what question should I ask?
- Would safe access or further documents change your view?

Write the answers into your decision register. If the response materially changes the written report, ask whether the inspector can confirm the clarification in writing.

## Repairs and costs need a defined scope
A repair number becomes useful once the cause, extent and intended remedy are reasonably clear. Ask whether a figure in the report is an estimate, an allowance or a contractor quotation. Keep urgent safety work, investigation costs, near-term repairs and ordinary maintenance in separate lines.

For the inspection fee and inclusions, see the [2026 inspection-cost examples and quote decoder](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-and-pest-inspection-cost). If you are still appointing someone, use the [inspector selection guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/how-to-choose-a-building-and-pest-inspector).

## Use the right deadline
Your useful deadline comes from the transaction: before signing, before a cooling-off period expires, or before bidding. Share material findings with your conveyancer or solicitor where they affect contract conditions, disclosure, settlement or the decision to proceed. At auction, work through the [five-gate due-diligence plan](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/auction-day-due-diligence) early enough to obtain specialist follow-up.

> Note: A good report does not make the decision for you. It gives you a dated set of observations, limitations and next questions so you can make the decision with your eyes open.

> Important: Urgent safety concerns and evidence of active water, pest activity or movement deserve prompt, property-specific advice. Avoid disturbing suspected hazardous material.

## Frequently asked questions
### What should I read first in a building inspection report?
Read the scope and access limitations first, followed by the significant findings and recommendations. This shows both what the inspector observed and what remains unknown.

### What does a major defect mean in a building inspection report?
Use the definition in the report and engagement agreement. Ask the inspector to explain the observed evidence, likely consequence and recommended next investigation for every major or significant item.

### Should I worry about a long list of minor defects?
Look for shared causes, active deterioration and accumulated cost. Many minor items can be manageable, while repeated moisture or movement signals may justify closer investigation.

### What if the roof space or subfloor was inaccessible?
Ask whether safe access and a return inspection can be arranged. If access remains unavailable, record the area as unresolved and decide how that uncertainty affects the purchase.

### Can a building inspector quote repair costs?
That depends on the agreed service and the inspector. Establish whether any figure is an estimate, allowance or contractor quotation, and seek a defined scope before relying on it.

### Who should investigate a structural concern?
Ask the inspector whether the observed issue warrants assessment by a suitably qualified structural engineer and what specific question the engineer should answer.

### Can I rely on a report supplied by the vendor or agent?
Check its date, scope, access, commissioning party, inspector, insurance and written purchaser-reliance or assignment terms. Commission your own work when those answers leave an important gap.

## Method
We turned the report into a decision register a buyer can keep: every finding traced to its consequence, its open question, the right professional and the deadline.

## Limitations
General reading guidance only. The report, engagement terms, property evidence, contract and advice from the relevant professional control the decision.

## Sources
- [AS 4349.1-2007 Inspection of buildings, Part 1: Pre-purchase inspections, residential buildings](https://store.standards.org.au/product/as-4349-1-2007) — Standards Australia; accessed 2026-07-20
- [Inspection reports before buying property](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/inspecting-a-property/inspection-reports) — NSW Government; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Pre-purchase inspection reports](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/property-professionals/working-as-an-agent/pre-purchase-inspection-reports) — NSW Government; accessed 2026-07-20
- [Inspect properties before you buy](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property/inspect-properties-before-you-buy) — Consumer Affairs Victoria; accessed 2026-07-20

### What each report can see
- **Desktop:** Everything on the record, and the questions it raises
- **Physical:** Everything reachable and visible, on the day
- **Together:** Better brief, better questions, fewer blind spots

_Neither can see inside a wall. Nothing can, without opening it._

sections.heading: What each report does
sections.markdown:
A desktop report asks *what is this building likely to need, and what should I check?* A physical inspection asks *what can be observed on site today?* The wider [property condition report guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/what-is-a-property-condition-report) explains related tenancy, insurance and dilapidation documents.

|  | Desktop report | Physical inspection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Based on | Listing, documents, public signals | On-site, hands-on examination |
| Answers | Likely exposure, what to ask, where to look | Actual visible defects, pests, moisture |
| Turnaround | Hours to a day | Days, booking plus report |
| Relative cost | A fraction of an inspection | Several times more |
| Best used | Early, across several properties | When you need certainty on one property |

sections.heading: What a desktop report can see
sections.markdown:
### What the available records can tell you

A desktop report works from visible signs, the era, the construction type, the documents you supply and the public signals around the address. It forecasts the repairs a home of this era and build is likely to be carrying, and points at the questions and inspections worth your money.

### What needs someone on site

Where access is safe, reasonable and included in the scope, an on-site inspector may enter the roof space or subfloor and use agreed tools on suspect areas. A physical inspection can reveal conditions no document records. Arrange one before an unconditional offer or auction when the property’s condition could change the decision.

sections.heading: Why running both, in order, works
sections.markdown:
Use the desktop read to form the inspection brief. The physical inspection can then target the era, construction and specific questions already identified.

### When you are weighing several properties

For a shortlist, run desktop reads early and commission physical inspections on the strongest candidates. See [what drives inspection cost](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-and-pest-inspection-cost) and [pre-auction inspection timing](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-inspection-before-auction).

> Note: Keep desktop findings, physical reports and later repairs together as one dated property record.

faqs.question: How does a desktop property report differ from a building inspection?
faqs.answer: A desktop report forecasts likely exposure from documents and public signals. A physical inspection examines accessible conditions on site.

faqs.question: Why pay for a desktop report if I'll get an inspection anyway?
faqs.answer: Because it does a different job: it gives you an independent picture of what the building is likely to need, and where an inspection should focus. If you're weighing several properties, it's also cheap enough to run on each, so the full inspection goes to the ones that matter.

faqs.question: When should I order each one?
faqs.answer: Run the desktop read early, for an independent picture of the building and to triage a shortlist. Commission the physical building and pest inspection when you need to confirm condition on site, and, if you are buying, before any unconditional offer or auction.

faqs.question: Can a desktop report find structural problems?
faqs.answer: It can flag visible or likely concerns and direct investigation. An on-site inspector or structural engineer provides property-specific assessment.

faqs.question: Do I still need a desktop report for a property I already plan to inspect?
faqs.answer: It can give the inspection direction, era-linked priorities and specific questions before you commit time and money to one property.

## Frequently asked questions
### How does a desktop property report differ from a building inspection?
A desktop report forecasts likely exposure from documents and public signals. A physical inspection examines accessible conditions on site.

### Why pay for a desktop report if I'll get an inspection anyway?
Because it does a different job: it gives you an independent picture of what the building is likely to need, and where an inspection should focus. If you're weighing several properties, it's also cheap enough to run on each, so the full inspection goes to the ones that matter.

### When should I order each one?
Run the desktop read early, for an independent picture of the building and to triage a shortlist. Commission the physical building and pest inspection when you need to confirm condition on site, and, if you are buying, before any unconditional offer or auction.

### Can a desktop report find structural problems?
It can flag visible or likely concerns and direct investigation. An on-site inspector or structural engineer provides property-specific assessment.

### Do I still need a desktop report for a property I already plan to inspect?
It can give the inspection direction, era-linked priorities and specific questions before you commit time and money to one property.

## Method
We compared what each kind of report can see, what it can reach, and which decisions it can honestly carry.

## Limitations
A desktop read cannot climb into the roof, give legal advice or diagnose a specialist problem. It tells you where to point the people who can.

guides.contentMarkdown:
# Property condition reports explained: which kind you need and what it costs

A property condition report is a snapshot of selected parts of a property at a particular time. The name can refer to a tenancy report, pre-purchase inspection, insurer survey, desktop review or dilapidation report. Its usefulness depends on why it was prepared, who commissioned it, what the author could access and who is allowed to rely on it.

## Research note
The label is context-dependent. For a purchase, official guidance focuses on a qualified pre-purchase inspection and the report's scope and exclusions; see [NSW inspection reports](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/inspecting-a-property/inspection-reports).

## Opening
### Start with why the report exists
- **Tenancy:** The bond’s evidence: condition at entry and exit
- **Purchase:** The buyer’s read: a pre-purchase building and pest inspection
- **Other uses:** Desktop reads, insurer surveys, dilapidation records

_One label, several documents. Purpose is how you tell them apart._

## One name, several documents
In Australia the same five words cover a tenancy form, a pre-purchase inspection, an insurer’s survey, a desktop read and a dilapidation record. Before comparing reports or prices, work out who ordered it, why, what it could reach, and who is allowed to rely on it.

**The condition-report family at a glance**

| Report | Who commissions it | The question it answers | Typical cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rental condition report | Landlord/agent and tenant, at entry and exit | What state was the property in when the tenancy started and ended? | Free, part of the tenancy process |
| Pre-purchase building inspection | The buyer | What visible defects and risks does this building have right now? | Roughly $400–$800 combined with pest, for a standard home |
| Desktop condition read | A buyer or owner | What is this building likely to need, and where should I look? | A fraction of a physical inspection |
| Insurance condition survey | The insurer, or the owner | What property information does this insurer require for underwriting or risk review? | Varies, confirm the insurer’s required scope |
| Dilapidation report | A developer or a neighbouring owner, before nearby works | What condition was this property in before construction started next door? | Quoted per property |
| Property condition assessment (commercial) | An investor or lender | What capital will this asset need over the holding period? | Scoped and quoted per asset |

## If you are renting: the report that protects your bond
For tenants, an entry condition report records the premises at the start of a tenancy under the applicable state or territory process. Review it by the deadline, add missing items, use clear dated photographs where permitted and keep a copy. At exit, it helps distinguish pre-existing condition, fair wear and tenant-caused damage. Follow the current tenancy authority instructions for the property's jurisdiction.

## If you are buying: the inspection kind
For a buyer, the relevant document is commonly a **pre-purchase building inspection**: an on-site, usually visual and non-invasive assessment of the agreed, safely accessible areas. The engagement should state timber-pest scope, the Australian Standard used, limitations and reliance rights. The [inspection quote guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-and-pest-inspection-cost) explains how to compare live, itemised quotes.

A **desktop condition read** uses era, construction, documents and public signals to triage a shortlist and direct later questions. A physical inspection then examines accessible conditions at the property. Read how the two work [in sequence](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/desktop-vs-physical-report).

## Insurance condition surveys
An insurer may request property information or its own survey before offering or renewing cover. Ask what document and evidence it requires before commissioning one. The [home condition and insurance guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/home-condition-and-insurance) covers underwriting, rebuild cost, exclusions, maintenance and evidence.

## Dilapidation reports: before the neighbours dig
A dilapidation report creates a dated baseline before nearby construction, demolition or excavation begins. It records existing cracks, paths and other relevant conditions for later comparison. Arrange it before work starts and pair it with [the wall-crack guide](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/cracks-structural-or-cosmetic).

## Property condition assessments: the commercial cousin
A *property condition assessment* is more common in commercial property, where investors and lenders assess an asset and its likely capital needs. For a home, maintain the equivalent evidence through [a current property record](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/keeping-a-record-of-your-home).

## Which one do you need?
- **Starting or ending a lease:** the rental condition report, done thoroughly, with photos.
- **Serious about buying a specific property:** the pre-purchase building and pest inspection.
- **Weighing several properties, or wanting an independent early read:** the desktop condition read.
- **Insurer asking questions, or an older home being priced for cover:** the insurance condition survey, plus a current condition record of your own.
- **Major construction starting next door:** the dilapidation report, arranged before the works begin.

> Note: A condition report is dated evidence. Keep it with later inspections, repairs, photographs and records so the next decision starts from the current building.

## Frequently asked questions
### What is a property condition report?
A written record of the condition of a property at a point in time. In Australia the term covers several different documents: the free rental condition report completed at the start and end of a tenancy, the pre-purchase building inspection a buyer commissions, a desktop condition read, an insurance condition survey, and a dilapidation report made before nearby construction. Which one you need depends on the decision it has to support.

### Is a property condition report the same as a building inspection?
For buyers, the phrase often means a pre-purchase building inspection. It also names rental entry and exit forms, insurance surveys and dilapidation reports, so confirm the purpose and scope.

### How much does a property condition report cost?
It depends entirely on which kind: the rental condition report is free as part of the tenancy process; a combined pre-purchase building and pest inspection runs roughly $400–$800 for a standard home; a desktop condition read costs a fraction of a physical inspection; insurance condition surveys and dilapidation reports are scoped and quoted, and insurance surveys are often arranged by the insurer.

### What is an insurance condition survey?
A property assessment requested or accepted for underwriting or risk review. Confirm the required scope with the insurer first. Policy wording and insurer assessment control the outcome.

### What is a property condition assessment?
Mostly a commercial-property term: an assessment, commissioned by an investor or lender, of an asset’s condition and the capital it is likely to need over a holding period. The residential equivalent of the habit is a current condition read of your home, kept up to date over time.

### Do I need a dilapidation report if construction is starting next door?
It creates a dated baseline for later comparison. Arrange it before excavation, demolition or construction begins.

## Method
We sorted the reports by purpose, commissioning party, reach and the decision each one supports.

## Limitations
General Australian guidance only. Contracts, statutes, policies, site conditions and professional scopes vary; obtain advice for the property and decision in front of you.

## Sources
- [Inspection reports before buying property](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/inspecting-a-property/inspection-reports) — NSW Government; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Choosing home insurance](https://moneysmart.gov.au/home-insurance/choosing-home-insurance) — Moneysmart, Australian Securities and Investments Commission; accessed 2026-07-19

Canonical guide: https://homechecker.com.au/guides/what-is-a-property-condition-report

guides.question: How much does a building biologist cost, and when might you need one?
guides.title: Building biologist cost in Australia: 2026 price examples
guides.summary: A building-biology quote can range from a focused mould investigation to a much broader healthy-home assessment. Three live price lists show what the fee may include and where the extras begin.
guides.answer: Published examples checked on 19 July 2026 included an $850 to $1,000 mould investigation with samples and a detailed report charged separately, a $990 assessment plus laboratory costs, and defined mould packages of about $970 and $1,660 including specified samples and a report. Ask for the whole expected fee in writing, including site time, moisture mapping, samples, laboratory work, the report, travel and any return visit.
guides.methodology: We drew the lines between moisture investigation, environmental sampling, medical advice and building inspection, then compared three providers’ published pricing so you can see how a quote is assembled.
guides.limitations: Take health concerns to a registered health practitioner and structural concerns to an appropriately qualified building professional.
guides.researchNote: For mould, health departments emphasise moisture control and medical advice for symptoms. The [National Training Register lists a current Advanced Diploma of Building Biology](https://training.gov.au/training/details/11429NAT). For electromagnetic fields, use [ARPANSA's evidence review](https://www.arpansa.gov.au/research-and-expertise/technical-reports/radiofrequency-electromagnetic-energy-and-health-research).

sections.heading: Opening
sections.markdown:
### Find the person who can answer your question
- **Building professional:** For defects, structure, drainage and moisture you can see
- **Environmental assessor:** For sampling and the indoor environment, with a defined scope
- **Health practitioner:** For symptoms and medical diagnosis

_If it is about your health, the right professional is medical._

sections.heading: Start with the question that is worrying you
sections.markdown:
“Building biologist” can mean moisture and mould investigation, indoor-air sampling, lead or chemical testing, electromagnetic-field measurement, drinking-water testing or a whole-home package. Tell each provider what you have noticed and what decision you need to make. That gives them a fair chance to quote the right work.

**Choose the professional by the decision you need to make**

| Question | Useful first professional | What the work should produce |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where is water entering or condensing? | Building inspector, building consultant or suitably experienced moisture investigator | Moisture pathway, affected materials, access limits and repair brief |
| What is present in air, dust or a surface? | Indoor environmental professional or occupational hygienist with an appropriate sampling plan | Defined method, chain of custody, laboratory result and interpretation limits |
| Has mould remediation achieved its scope? | Independent post-remediation verifier | Pre-agreed acceptance criteria and verification report |
| Are symptoms connected with the home? | Registered health practitioner | Medical assessment informed by relevant building results |
| Is cracking, movement or another defect structurally significant? | Building inspector, then structural engineer if indicated | Building evidence and, where required, engineering diagnosis |

sections.heading: Current published pricing
sections.markdown:
We checked these provider pages on 19 July 2026. The scopes vary considerably, which is exactly why the detail beside the price matters.

**Published mould and building-biology price examples, accessed 19 July 2026**

| Provider example | Published fee | Important inclusions or additions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Building Biology NSW](https://buildingbiologynsw.com.au/service/the-complete-healthy-home-inspection/) | $850 single storey; up to $1,000 double storey | $140 per laboratory sample; comprehensive report listed separately at $850 |
| [Wave Building Biology](https://www.wavebuildingbiology.com.au/prices) | $990 including GST | Laboratory analysis added at $120 per sample |
| [Buildingbiology Services Australia](https://buildingbiologyservices.com/mould-inspection) | About $970 standard; $1,660 detailed | Each example specifies consultation, samples, laboratory analysis, report and recommendations; travel is additional |

Property size, access, site time, sample count, laboratory fees, travel, report depth, urgency and return visits determine the final cost. Give each consultant the same written problem and ask for the complete expected fee.

sections.heading: The quote checklist
sections.markdown:
- **Question and scope:** the rooms, history, suspected pathway and decision the report must support.
- **Investigation method:** visual inspection, moisture meter, thermal imaging, borescope, sampling or another defined method, and its limitations.
- **Sampling plan:** sample type, number, locations, controls, independent laboratory, chain of custody and the fee for each additional sample.
- **Deliverable:** verbal advice, short findings, comprehensive report, repair scope or post-remediation criteria.
- **Independence:** whether the assessor also sells remediation, products or follow-on work.
- **Professional standing:** relevant training, experience, professional indemnity and the laboratory’s accreditation for the analysis requested.

sections.heading: Check training and laboratory scope
sections.markdown: The [current 11429NAT Advanced Diploma of Building Biology](https://training.gov.au/training/details/11429NAT) is a nationally accredited qualification and is recognised by the Australasian Society of Building Biologists as a professional benchmark. Ask which training and experience apply to the service you need. For laboratory work, confirm that the laboratory's accreditation covers the requested analysis, then require the sampling method, chain of custody and interpretation limits in the report.

sections.heading: Mould: find moisture before chasing species
sections.markdown:
Mould growth requires moisture. [NSW Health](https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/environment/factsheets/Pages/mould.aspx) and the [Victorian Department of Health](https://www.betterhealth.vic.gov.au/health/conditionsandtreatments/mould-and-your-health) emphasise moisture control and safe clean-up. Use sampling for a defined purpose such as characterising contamination, documenting a dispute or checking remediation.

A DIY culture plate will happily grow the spores that live in every Australian home, which proves very little. Start with [the moisture pathway](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/damp-and-moisture-in-your-home), then add a defined sampling plan where it will change the decision.

sections.heading: EMF measurement and health questions
sections.markdown: An instrument can measure an electromagnetic field. The question that matters is what the reading is being compared against. [ARPANSA reviews radiofrequency health research](https://www.arpansa.gov.au/research-and-expertise/technical-reports/radiofrequency-electromagnetic-energy-and-health-research) and publishes Australian exposure guidance. For EMF work, require the quantity, instrument, calibration, frequency range, measurement protocol and comparison standard. Take medical questions to a health practitioner.

sections.heading: When specialist environmental work is proportionate
sections.markdown:
- **Recurring or widespread mould** where the water source or affected extent remains unclear.
- **A concealed or complex water event**, including a flood, long-running leak or contaminated cavity.
- **A formal dispute, insurance or remediation process** that needs an agreed sampling or verification protocol.
- **A vulnerable occupant** where a health practitioner wants better environmental information to support clinical care.
- **A specific exposure question** that can be measured against a recognised method and standard.

For an ordinary pre-purchase decision, start with a qualified [building and pest inspection](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-and-pest-inspection-cost). Add environmental work for specific questions left unresolved.

> Important: Seek medical advice for symptoms, urgent health advice for significant exposure concerns and appropriately qualified building advice for defects.

faqs.question: How much does a building biologist cost in Australia?
faqs.answer: Published examples checked on 19 July 2026 included $850 to $1,000 before samples and a detailed report, $990 before laboratory costs, and defined mould packages of about $970 and $1,660. The final cost depends heavily on the samples, report and property scope.

faqs.question: What should a building biologist quote include?
faqs.answer: Request site time, rooms or areas, investigation methods, moisture mapping, sample count, laboratory fees, written report, travel, urgency and any return verification as separate line items.

faqs.question: What qualification can I check?
faqs.answer: 11429NAT Advanced Diploma of Building Biology is a current nationally accredited qualification recognised by the Australasian Society of Building Biologists as a professional benchmark.

faqs.question: Can a building biologist diagnose why someone is unwell?
faqs.answer: A registered health practitioner diagnoses and treats health conditions. An environmental consultant can investigate and measure defined building conditions.

faqs.question: Is EMF testing evidence that a home caused symptoms?
faqs.answer: Measurement can be compared with an identified exposure standard. Medical causation belongs with a health practitioner. ARPANSA is the Australian authority for radiation protection guidance.

faqs.question: Should I get mould testing before buying?
faqs.answer: Use testing for a defined question that can change the purchase decision or remediation scope. First identify visible moisture, leaks and affected materials through the appropriate building inspection.

# Building biologist cost in Australia: 2026 price examples

Published examples checked on 19 July 2026 included an $850 to $1,000 mould investigation with samples and a detailed report charged separately, a $990 assessment plus laboratory costs, and defined mould packages of about $970 and $1,660 including specified samples and a report. Ask for the whole expected fee in writing, including site time, moisture mapping, samples, laboratory work, the report, travel and any return visit.

## Research note
For mould, health departments emphasise moisture control and medical advice for symptoms. The [National Training Register lists a current Advanced Diploma of Building Biology](https://training.gov.au/training/details/11429NAT). For electromagnetic fields, use [ARPANSA's evidence review](https://www.arpansa.gov.au/research-and-expertise/technical-reports/radiofrequency-electromagnetic-energy-and-health-research).

## Opening
### Find the person who can answer your question
- **Building professional:** For defects, structure, drainage and moisture you can see
- **Environmental assessor:** For sampling and the indoor environment, with a defined scope
- **Health practitioner:** For symptoms and medical diagnosis

_If it is about your health, the right professional is medical._

## Start with the question that is worrying you
“Building biologist” can mean moisture and mould investigation, indoor-air sampling, lead or chemical testing, electromagnetic-field measurement, drinking-water testing or a whole-home package. Tell each provider what you have noticed and what decision you need to make. That gives them a fair chance to quote the right work.

**Choose the professional by the decision you need to make**

| Question | Useful first professional | What the work should produce |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where is water entering or condensing? | Building inspector, building consultant or suitably experienced moisture investigator | Moisture pathway, affected materials, access limits and repair brief |
| What is present in air, dust or a surface? | Indoor environmental professional or occupational hygienist with an appropriate sampling plan | Defined method, chain of custody, laboratory result and interpretation limits |
| Has mould remediation achieved its scope? | Independent post-remediation verifier | Pre-agreed acceptance criteria and verification report |
| Are symptoms connected with the home? | Registered health practitioner | Medical assessment informed by relevant building results |
| Is cracking, movement or another defect structurally significant? | Building inspector, then structural engineer if indicated | Building evidence and, where required, engineering diagnosis |

## Current published pricing
We checked these provider pages on 19 July 2026. The scopes vary considerably, which is exactly why the detail beside the price matters.

**Published mould and building-biology price examples, accessed 19 July 2026**

| Provider example | Published fee | Important inclusions or additions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Building Biology NSW](https://buildingbiologynsw.com.au/service/the-complete-healthy-home-inspection/) | $850 single storey; up to $1,000 double storey | $140 per laboratory sample; comprehensive report listed separately at $850 |
| [Wave Building Biology](https://www.wavebuildingbiology.com.au/prices) | $990 including GST | Laboratory analysis added at $120 per sample |
| [Buildingbiology Services Australia](https://buildingbiologyservices.com/mould-inspection) | About $970 standard; $1,660 detailed | Each example specifies consultation, samples, laboratory analysis, report and recommendations; travel is additional |

Property size, access, site time, sample count, laboratory fees, travel, report depth, urgency and return visits determine the final cost. Give each consultant the same written problem and ask for the complete expected fee.

## The quote checklist
- **Question and scope:** the rooms, history, suspected pathway and decision the report must support.
- **Investigation method:** visual inspection, moisture meter, thermal imaging, borescope, sampling or another defined method, and its limitations.
- **Sampling plan:** sample type, number, locations, controls, independent laboratory, chain of custody and the fee for each additional sample.
- **Deliverable:** verbal advice, short findings, comprehensive report, repair scope or post-remediation criteria.
- **Independence:** whether the assessor also sells remediation, products or follow-on work.
- **Professional standing:** relevant training, experience, professional indemnity and the laboratory’s accreditation for the analysis requested.

## Check training and laboratory scope
The [current 11429NAT Advanced Diploma of Building Biology](https://training.gov.au/training/details/11429NAT) is a nationally accredited qualification and is recognised by the Australasian Society of Building Biologists as a professional benchmark. Ask which training and experience apply to the service you need. For laboratory work, confirm that the laboratory's accreditation covers the requested analysis, then require the sampling method, chain of custody and interpretation limits in the report.

## Mould: find moisture before chasing species
Mould growth requires moisture. [NSW Health](https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/environment/factsheets/Pages/mould.aspx) and the [Victorian Department of Health](https://www.betterhealth.vic.gov.au/health/conditionsandtreatments/mould-and-your-health) emphasise moisture control and safe clean-up. Use sampling for a defined purpose such as characterising contamination, documenting a dispute or checking remediation.

A DIY culture plate will happily grow the spores that live in every Australian home, which proves very little. Start with [the moisture pathway](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/damp-and-moisture-in-your-home), then add a defined sampling plan where it will change the decision.

## EMF measurement and health questions
An instrument can measure an electromagnetic field. The question that matters is what the reading is being compared against. [ARPANSA reviews radiofrequency health research](https://www.arpansa.gov.au/research-and-expertise/technical-reports/radiofrequency-electromagnetic-energy-and-health-research) and publishes Australian exposure guidance. For EMF work, require the quantity, instrument, calibration, frequency range, measurement protocol and comparison standard. Take medical questions to a health practitioner.

## When specialist environmental work is proportionate
- **Recurring or widespread mould** where the water source or affected extent remains unclear.
- **A concealed or complex water event**, including a flood, long-running leak or contaminated cavity.
- **A formal dispute, insurance or remediation process** that needs an agreed sampling or verification protocol.
- **A vulnerable occupant** where a health practitioner wants better environmental information to support clinical care.
- **A specific exposure question** that can be measured against a recognised method and standard.

For an ordinary pre-purchase decision, start with a qualified [building and pest inspection](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-and-pest-inspection-cost). Add environmental work for specific questions left unresolved.

> Important: Seek medical advice for symptoms, urgent health advice for significant exposure concerns and appropriately qualified building advice for defects.

## Frequently asked questions
### How much does a building biologist cost in Australia?
Published examples checked on 19 July 2026 included $850 to $1,000 before samples and a detailed report, $990 before laboratory costs, and defined mould packages of about $970 and $1,660. The final cost depends heavily on the samples, report and property scope.

### What should a building biologist quote include?
Request site time, rooms or areas, investigation methods, moisture mapping, sample count, laboratory fees, written report, travel, urgency and any return verification as separate line items.

### What qualification can I check?
11429NAT Advanced Diploma of Building Biology is a current nationally accredited qualification recognised by the Australasian Society of Building Biologists as a professional benchmark.

### Can a building biologist diagnose why someone is unwell?
A registered health practitioner diagnoses and treats health conditions. An environmental consultant can investigate and measure defined building conditions.

### Is EMF testing evidence that a home caused symptoms?
Measurement can be compared with an identified exposure standard. Medical causation belongs with a health practitioner. ARPANSA is the Australian authority for radiation protection guidance.

### Should I get mould testing before buying?
Use testing for a defined question that can change the purchase decision or remediation scope. First identify visible moisture, leaks and affected materials through the appropriate building inspection.

## Method
We drew the lines between moisture investigation, environmental sampling, medical advice and building inspection, then compared three providers’ published pricing so you can see how a quote is assembled.

## Limitations
Take health concerns to a registered health practitioner and structural concerns to an appropriately qualified building professional.

## Sources
- [Mould](https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/environment/factsheets/Pages/mould.aspx) — NSW Health; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Mould and your health](https://www.betterhealth.vic.gov.au/health/conditionsandtreatments/mould-and-your-health) — Better Health Channel, Victorian Department of Health; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Radiofrequency electromagnetic energy and health research](https://www.arpansa.gov.au/research-and-expertise/technical-reports/radiofrequency-electromagnetic-energy-and-health-research) — ARPANSA; accessed 2026-07-19
- [11429NAT Advanced Diploma of Building Biology](https://training.gov.au/training/details/11429NAT) — National Training Register; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Mould investigation pricing](https://buildingbiologynsw.com.au/service/the-complete-healthy-home-inspection/) — Building Biology NSW; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Prices](https://www.wavebuildingbiology.com.au/prices) — Wave Building Biology; accessed 2026-07-19
- [Mould inspection fees](https://buildingbiologyservices.com/mould-inspection) — Buildingbiology Services Australia; accessed 2026-07-19

sections.heading: Opening
sections.markdown:
### Know when your clock starts and stops
- **Trigger:** Signing, exchange or receipt: each state picks its own starting gun
- **Deadline:** Counted in clear, business or working days, and it matters which
- **Exceptions:** Auctions, waivers and edge cases can switch it off entirely

_Get your actual deadline, for your actual contract, in writing._

sections.heading: The state-by-state orientation
sections.markdown:
This table covers the usual residential private-sale position for an individual buyer. Auctions, off-the-plan contracts, options, corporate buyers, rural or commercial land, written waivers and contract amendments can change the result. Have the actual deadline confirmed.

**Residential cooling-off orientation, legal review is still required for the actual contract**

| State / territory | Headline period | Typical consequence of withdrawal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NSW | 5 business days after exchange; 10 business days for off-the-plan contracts | 0.25% of the purchase price |
| VIC | 3 clear business days, beginning when the buyer signs | The greater of $100 or 0.2% of the purchase price |
| QLD | 5 business days, triggered by the buyer receiving the fully signed contract | Seller may deduct up to 0.25% of the purchase price |
| ACT | 5 working days | 0.25% of the purchase price |
| NT | 4 business days in the usual eligible transaction | No statutory penalty stated in the standard government guidance |
| SA | 2 clear business days; the Form 1 timing matters | Seller generally retains the prescribed amount, commonly $100 |
| WA | No general statutory cooling-off period for an ordinary private sale | Any exit depends on negotiated contract conditions |
| TAS | No general statutory cooling-off period for an ordinary private sale | Any exit depends on negotiated contract conditions |

sections.heading: Each state starts the clock differently
sections.markdown:
In Victoria, the [three-clear-business-day period begins on the date the buyer signs](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property/buying-property-by-private-sale). In NSW, the [five-business-day period starts at exchange](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/contracts-and-deposits) and ends at 5 pm on the fifth business day after the day of exchange. In Queensland, the [clock starts when the buyer receives the contract signed by both parties](https://www.qld.gov.au/community/fair-trading/regulated-industries-licensing-and-legislation/property-industry-regulation/legal-requirements-for-the-property-industry/cooling-off-period-for-residential-property-contracts).

In South Australia, cooling-off is connected to service of the statutory Form 1 and the contract. Ask your legal representative to state the deadline, time and notice method in writing.

sections.heading: Auction and near-auction exceptions
sections.markdown:
A purchase made at auction generally has no cooling-off period. The edges differ. Victoria also excludes a private sale made within three clear business days before or after a publicly advertised auction. NSW excludes exchange on the auction day after the property is passed in. Queensland excludes a follow-up sale after an unsuccessful auction if it occurs before 5 pm on the second business day and the buyer was a registered bidder. Those rules are why an auction calendar can matter even when the final negotiation looks like a private sale.

If an auction is in the picture, finish the contract, finance and building work before you bid. Use the [auction due-diligence checklist](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/auction-day-due-diligence) and the narrower guide to [pre-auction building inspections](https://homechecker.com.au/guides/building-inspection-before-auction).

sections.heading: Waiving, shortening or changing the period
sections.markdown: Some regimes allow the buyer to waive or shorten the period through a prescribed mechanism. [NSW uses a section 66W certificate](https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/buying-and-selling-property/buying-property-nsw/contracts-and-deposits) from the buyer's solicitor or conveyancer. [Queensland permits a written waiver or shortening](https://www.qld.gov.au/community/fair-trading/regulated-industries-licensing-and-legislation/property-industry-regulation/legal-requirements-for-the-property-industry/cooling-off-period-for-residential-property-contracts). A waiver removes or shortens the buyer's statutory cooling-off right, so the right to rescind may end as soon as the prescribed waiver takes effect.

sections.heading: Contract conditions in WA and Tasmania
sections.markdown: WA and Tasmania have no general statutory cooling-off period for ordinary private sales. Use appropriately drafted contract conditions for finance, building and pest, sale of another property or due diligence. The [WA Government advises buyers to understand the contract before signing](https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/buying-property-private-sale). Have each condition drafted or reviewed professionally.

sections.heading: What to do inside a cooling-off window
sections.markdown:
1. **Have the contract and disclosure bundle reviewed**, including title, plan, easements, covenants, planning controls, notices and settlement terms.
2. **Confirm finance against this property**, including valuation or lender conditions still outstanding.
3. **Complete the physical checks** the property warrants within the available time.
4. **Escalate specific flags** to an engineer, electrician, plumber, strata specialist or other appropriate professional.
5. **Keep the deadline and notice method in writing**, using the method your legal representative confirms.

> Important: Cooling-off law is jurisdiction- and contract-specific. This comparison is current to 19 July 2026. Have a conveyancer or solicitor confirm eligibility, the exact expiry time, the required notice and the financial consequence.
